mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility over the past four weeks indicates more time spent at home, substituting for retail and recreation trips, and will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.0 to 10.3 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-28-day mean rises above its last-28-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to increase week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT mobility drops by more than 4 points in a single week, it signals reduced commuting and errand trips that directly feed into fewer retail visits the following week, pulling RETAIL_REC down.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 4 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -16.0 to -20.1 (4.1 point drop) in the latest week, coincident with RETAIL_REC falling from -16.3 to -21.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a greater-than-4-point weekly drop in TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility compound to reduce overall out-of-home activity, producing a larger negative effect on RETAIL_REC than either series alone, over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT declined in the most recent week after two weeks of relative stability
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's two-week-ahead mean does not fall when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT decline simultaneously week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of rising RESIDENTIAL and falling GROCERY_PHARM mobility signals a renewed tightening-restrictions regime, under which RETAIL_REC will continue trending downward over the next four weeks as non-essential retail activity is curtailed.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 22.4 to 15.6 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 8.6 to 10.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week-ahead mean rises even though RESIDENTIAL keeps rising and GROCERY_PHARM keeps falling.

mechanism_narrative: As the season transitions toward colder autumn weather in mid-October, outdoor PARKS mobility declines seasonally, pushing displaced outdoor activity indoors and modestly boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as shopping substitutes for park visits.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell sharply from -13.4 to -24.9 in the latest week, consistent with seasonal cooling
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's 4-week-ahead mean falls alongside continued PARKS decline rather than rising.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-week drop in RETAIL_REC exceeding 4 points relative to its prior two-week average represents a transient shock rather than a trend break, and mobility will mean-revert upward over the following week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC's weekly value falls more than 4 points below the prior two-week average
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from a two-week average of about -16.1 to -21.0 in the latest week, a drop of nearly 5 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat in the week after a sharp single-week drop, rather than reverting upward.

mechanism_narrative: A combined decline in GROCERY_PHARM alongside rising RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates renewed caution around errand and shopping trips broadly, which will disproportionately suppress discretionary RETAIL_REC visits over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined 6.8 points while RESIDENTIAL rose 1.7 points in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's two-week-ahead mean rises despite continued GROCERY_PHARM decline and RESIDENTIAL increase.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized in a narrow band around -15 to -17 for three consecutive weeks, indicating a steady commuting baseline that will keep RETAIL_REC roughly flat to slightly negative over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES values were -16.6, -15.3, -15.1 over the last three weeks, a narrow range
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-week value rises more than 3 points even though WORKPLACES remains within its stable band.
